profile.headline: Weather Software Engineer
profile.summary: Leveraging deep expertise in meteorology and computer science, I specialize in developing cutting-edge AI and cloud-based technologies for real-time weather data processing. My proficiency in leading complex technical programs, designing high-performance architectures, and creating groundbreaking tools has consistently driven advancements in weather forecasting and significantly improved team efficiency.

positions.title: Weather Visualization and AI Research Development Branch Chief - Global Systems Laboratory
positions.description:
Project manager and lead senior software engineer for various programs, including developing machine learning and deep learning algorithms to efficiently process high-volume data and extract high-value information from weather and climate data, creating visualization and interactive environments to enhance understanding of complex scientific problems, developing and researching services and capabilities on commercial cloud service providers, and developing information systems to deliver and distribute high-volume data efficiently for interactive programs and research: 
* Lead cloud development activities investigating ways to create event-driven, asynchronous architecture to process data through cloud services.
* Developed a cloud-based Kubernetes cluster using Terraform that leverages spot prices for compute instances, reducing costs by 60%-70% compared to traditional systems. This cluster is used for processing ensemble data to deliver actionable information to end users in near real-time and is designed to handle high-density and exascale data in the future. In early 2024, I led the transition of this capability to the National Weather Service.
* Successfully developed, planned, and tracked the transition of AI technology to detect tropical cyclones from model and satellite data to the European Center for Medium-range Weather Forecasting.
* Designed and developed deep learning AI processes using TensorFlow and PyTorch to process satellite observations and atmospheric weather model data for multiple projects, including tropical cyclone tracking, convection initiation, satellite-based soil moisture product, air quality observations, and atmospheric radiative transfer parameterization.
* Successfully planned, tracked, and executed the operational transition of the Science on a Sphere program to the NOAA’s Office of Education. The first transition to education for NOAA.

positions.title: Chief, Informatics and Visualization Section - Global Systems Laboratory
positions.description:
Informatics and Visualization branch chief and senior software engineer for designing, analyzing, and development of applications for visualizing, processing, and manipulating geophysical data.
* Designed and developed a machine learning process using the U-Net model to identify key areas within satellite imagery for targeted data extraction and assimilation for modeling.
* Project manager and lead software engineer for the NOAA Earth Information System (NEIS)/TerraViz program creating visualization and interactive environment simulations to help and encourage understanding of complex scientific problems.
* Plan and manage Informatics and Visualization section projects, schedules, milestones, staff, and resource allocations.
* Project manager and lead software engineer for various programs for visualization, processing, and data delivery of complex scientific data.
* Work with other partners across NCAR, Navy, and Department of Energy, to develop strategies for using machine learning for model data assimilation.
* Co-lead internal group to help with professional development, mentorship, facilitating tasks and communication to and from Senior Management to Projects across the division.
* Designed and led the development of high-performance processing infrastructure to remotely process high-resolution model data and send the results to users, limiting bandwidth required to access data.
* Developed implementation, maintenance, and automation plans for services using Docker containers and Ansible.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer Team Lead - Global Systems Laboratory
positions.description:
• Served as temporary lead for High Impact Weather Prediction Project (HIWPP) Test Program where I coordinated tasks and efforts with NOAA research laboratories and other outside groups including NCAR and the Navy to develop the HIWPP Test Program project plan, including deliverables, milestones, budgets and resource allocations.
• Project manager and lead software engineer for NOAA Earth Information System(NEIS)/TerraViz program creating visualization and interactive environment simulations to help and encourage understanding of complex scientific problems.
• Software engineer for Science on a Sphere (SOS) program creating visualizations, content, and tools for education of scientific data and processes.
• Designed and developed architecture for new systems, visualizations, simulations, and prototypes.
• Design and develop plans for future growth, system maintenance, and software transition.
• Developed capability to allow Science on a Sphere to load data remotely hosted through the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) Web Map Service (WMS)
• Designed and Developed and maintained back-end services for the NEIS project to harvest various data set metadata and provide standard protocol allowing TerraViz visualization client to discover, access, and integrate a variety of NOAA dat asets scattered across NOAA enterprise
• Designed and developed high performance data ingest system using Apache Storm and Hazelcast.
• Coordinate large scale cross agency technology demonstrations.
• Implemented and maintained continuous integration system using Apache Jenkins.
• Served as member of several committees within laboratory to provide technical guidance and oversight for other laboratory projects.

positions.title: Technical Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
Led design, analysis, and development of applications for visualizing, processing, and manipulating geophysical data.
• Led software engineer on Global Systems Division NextGen program creating, testing, and evaluating data access and content delivery framework
• Led software engineer for FX-Net, Gridded FX-Net, Grid Extraction Tool programs creating client/server applications to deliver real-time weather data quickly and efficiently to remote systems along with developing interactive visualization and data manipulation applications for these data.
• Led research, design, and development for Gridded FX-Net, which resulted in funding for prototype development, and ongoing support.
• Designed and developed architecture for new systems, visualizations, simulations, and prototypes.
• Designed and developed plans for future growth, system maintenance, and software transition.
• Created and taught training programs for FX-Net and Gridded FX-Net applications.
• Served as member of several committees within laboratory to provide technical guidance and oversight for other laboratory projects.
• Planned system administration activities including maintenance and management of several Linux servers.
• Gathered and processed new meteorological data sets for FX-Net data servers.
• Interacted with customers providing support and soliciting feedback to improve applications.
• Created application frameworks for team using SOAP and Java.
• Designed, developed, and implemented web services to adhere to OGC Specifications.
• Presented white papers at various conferences and meetings.

positions.title: Web Developer/IT Consultant (Volunteer)
positions.description:
Design and develop web pages and provide technical consulting.
• Assist design and development of company's website.
• Provide IT guidance and systems support.
• Built ticket purchase and management system for website.
• Created cell phone voting system and related web pages for certain performances.

positions.title: Programmer/Analyst
positions.description:
Designed and developed web applications for data visualization and processing configuration management.
• Designed and developed web site including web applications and data display products.
• Developed web applications to access, organize, and display geophysical data from databases and files.
• Designed, implemented, and repaired software used for data ingest, data processing, and system monitoring.
• Performed system administration activities including maintenance and management of several Linux servers.
• Monitored, maintained, and developed network of meteorological equipment for real-time data and stability.
• Assembled and delivered data in different formats including netCDF, NOAA Bufr messages, and Comma Separated Values (CSV) files.
• Prepared and presented presentations regarding our work for interested parties and conventions.

projects.title: Science On a Sphere (SOS)
projects.description: Science On a Sphere® (SOS) is a room sized, global display system that uses computers and video projectors to display planetary data onto a six foot diameter sphere, analogous to a giant animated globe. Researchers at NOAA developed Science On a Sphere® as an educational tool to help illustrate Earth System science to people of all ages. Animated images of atmospheric storms, climate change, and ocean temperature can be shown on the sphere, which is used to explain what are sometimes complex environmental processes, in a way that is simultaneously intuitive and captivating.

projects.title: NOAA Earth Information System (NEIS)
projects.description: NOAA Earth Information System (NEIS) is a modular framework of layered services designed to help NOAA’s mission areas by facilitating the discovery, access, integration, and under-standing of all NOAA (past, present, and future).
